newsitem.title: USA: Drug helps prevent bone disease in steroid patients.
newsitem.headline: Drug helps prevent bone disease in steroid patients.

text.p: A drug that inhibits the recycling of bone in the body may prevent brittle bone disease among people who need to take steroid treatments, according to a new study published in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine.
The drug is etidronate, sold under the brand name Didronel by MGI Pharma in Minneapolis, Minn..

In tests on people who were taking steroids for a variety of conditions, 67 of whom received etidronate and 74 who received a placebo, researchers found that etidronate increased the density of some bones while placebo recipients saw their bones become more brittle.
The research team, led by Dr. Jonathan Adachi of McMaster University in Hamilton, Ontario, gave etidronate for 14 days and calcium supplements for another 76 days before the cycle was repeated.

"We found that one year of treatment with etidronate and calcium prevented bone loss and vertebral fractures in patients with a variety of disorders who were taking corticosteroids," Adachi and his colleagues concluded.

"It is now clear that we do not have to accept bone loss and high fracture rates as inevitable consequences of high dose glucocorticoid therapy," said Dr. Ian Reid of the University of Auckland in an editorial in the Journal.
He said people who are starting long-term treatment with steroid drugs should have their bone density measured. Patients whose bones register on the low side of average should be offered the drug.
